name: Companion
description: A coding agent you call up: hold ⌃⌥ in any app and speak (drag to draw), let go and it answers by your pointer. In a note, write @claude to ask it something, or @ and a name to start another (@opus, @codex, @opus-review): it answers in bubbles, comments on lines (cards in the margin), suggests changes you take with Tab, proposes larger ones you take change by change, or writes with you. Always-on sessions on this machine: Claude Code's run in the app (its chat), Codex's and OpenCode's in terminals.

mode.label: Mode

labels.pair: Pair: with you as you write

mode.description: how much it does: off; quiet, it answers only what you ask it (@claude in a note, Ask companion); pair, it also sees what you write when you pause, answers what's meant for it as a person in the room would, and may write in your notes

agent.label: Agent
agent.description: the coding agent its session runs (claude, codex, opencode, claude_personal...)

name.label: Name
name.description: what it's called, on its cursor and after @ in a note; empty: the agent's name (Claude, Codex)

model.label: Model
model.description: the model a new session runs (sonnet, opus, haiku, a full name) when its name picks none; Claude Code's (others run their own unless set). A quicker one answers sooner

effort.label: Effort
effort.description: how hard its model thinks (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) when its name picks none; Claude Code's (others run their own unless set). Less answers sooner

summoned_model.label: Model for summoned asks
summoned_model.description: what answers its Talk key (on screen, or in the app at the pointer): a session of its own on this model, kept warm with a short prompt, apart from the one that watches your notes (Claude Code's). The companion's own: that one answers them too

profiles.label: Names
profiles.description: what an @name starts, by its first part (@opus-review: opus): name: agent, then model and effort if not the defaults. Yours add to these, or change one by its name

comments.label: Comments
comments.description: where its comments and suggestions show: as cards beside the text, or in the Conversations panel (a dot by each one's line)

pause.label: Pause before it looks
pause.description: seconds without typing mid-sentence before it sees what you wrote (Pair); a sentence's end goes after a breath, Enter and a question at once

private.label: Private
private.description: what it never sees: a folder of notes (nothing you do there reaches it, nor does a note with companion: private in its properties), a site (site: bank.com, its subdomains too), a Browser container (container: <id>) or an app (app: <bundle id>, kept from it by the helper). Starts with password managers and banks

keys.label: Talk keys
keys.description: on a Mac, the keys that call it up at your pointer, in any app: hold one and speak (drag to draw on the screen), let go and it answers there; a tap opens a box to type in, a double tap listens hands-free until the next. These keys never dictate

voice.label: Voice
voice.description: on a Mac, whether it answers out loud by your pointer: when you asked by voice (its Talk key held, or said into its box), always (a typed ask too), or never. its voice is the Voice provider's, else this Mac's

sounds.label: Sounds
sounds.description: on a Mac, soft short sounds as you summon it with its Talk key, let go, and as its answer comes

quiet_on_calls.label: Quiet on calls
quiet_on_calls.description: on a Mac, while another app uses the microphone (a call in Zoom, FaceTime, Meet, Slack or Discord, a recording), its answers show as text with a play button instead of being said, and it makes no sounds; your Talk key still works

hide_from_shares.label: Hidden from screen shares
hide_from_shares.description: on a Mac, its cursors, drawings, cards and boxes stay out of screen shares, recordings and screenshots: only you see them

voice_name.label: Soniox voice
voice_name.description: the Soniox voice it speaks with (Adrian, Hazel, Logan, Larissa...: each speaks every language; Soniox's console lists them under Text-to-speech, Voices)

voice_provider.label: Voice provider
voice_provider.description: whose cloud voice speaks first (the other takes over if it fails, then this Mac's): automatic is ElevenLabs' once this machine has its key (vau voice key), else Soniox's

elevenlabs_voice.label: ElevenLabs voice
elevenlabs_voice.description: the ElevenLabs voice's id (Brian: nPczCjzI2devNBz1zQrb, Sarah: EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL; ElevenLabs' Voices page has each one's)

elevenlabs_model.label: ElevenLabs model
elevenlabs_model.description: the ElevenLabs model it speaks with (eleven_flash_v2_5: the quickest)

voice_speed.label: Voice speed
voice_speed.description: how fast it speaks, times the usual

voice_front.label: Voice front

labels.realtime: Realtime: it hears you and answers at once

voice_front.description: on a Mac, how its Talk key's spoken asks are answered: realtime, a speech-to-speech model (OpenAI's, once this machine has its key: vau voice key --provider openai) that answers small talk itself and asks the summoned model about your screen; or your words dictated, the summoned model's answer said by the voice above. Without the key, or should it fail, the second

realtime_model.label: Realtime model
realtime_model.description: the OpenAI Realtime model it talks with (gpt-realtime-2.1-mini: the quickest and cheapest; gpt-realtime-2.1)

realtime_voice.label: Realtime voice
realtime_voice.description: the OpenAI voice it talks in (cedar, marin, alloy, ash, ballad, coral, echo, sage, shimmer, verse)

island.label: Agents by the notch
island.description: on a Mac, the agents working in the background (terminal agents, jobs) show as one quiet count beside the notch (top centre with none), orange only when one waits on you; what they ask comes up there at a pause (Answer, or Not now to put it off), and a hover lists them

job_news.label: Job news

labels.quiet: A silent notification when one needs you or fails; one ready knocks by the notch
labels.spoken: Said aloud too, a ready one's knock as well

job_news.description: how it tells you of its jobs: one ready knocks by the notch (Ready to show you, its proof shown when you say show me); aloud only when spoken (while you're at this Mac: its Talk key held in the last 15 minutes, not in a focus block). Jobs lists them all either way

jobs_agent.label: Jobs' agent
jobs_agent.description: the Claude Code its jobs run as, with its account if not the default one (claude_personal): a handoff asking for Codex or OpenCode runs that instead

jobs_model.label: Jobs' model
jobs_model.description: the model a Claude Code job runs (opus, sonnet, a full name)

jobs_effort.label: Jobs' effort
jobs_effort.description: how hard a Claude Code job thinks (low, medium, high, xhigh, max)

jobs_mode.label: Jobs' permissions

labels.auto: Auto: it asks only for what's risky

jobs_mode.description: how much a Claude Code job does without asking you (what it asks waits in its terminal and the menu bar's Jobs as needs you)

jobs_land.label: Jobs land themselves
jobs_land.description: a coding job whose checks pass merges its change itself (as its repo's rules say) and cleans up its worktree, instead of waiting ready for your review; it asks only on a real tradeoff, and its demo is still there to watch

jobs_never.label: Never run jobs in
jobs_never.description: folders a job never runs in on this vault's machines, each with why (~/Work/Acme: Acme's work runs on its own machine): a handoff there is refused, saying why

jobs_machine.label: Jobs' machine
jobs_machine.description: where a job runs when nothing ties it to a machine (a note, research, a GitHub page checked out there): auto, an always-on machine serving this vault (its server on its own, not in a laptop's app) while one is online; here; or a machine's id (Machines lists them). A preview, an editor's project or a repo a job names goes there too when that machine has its repo checked out and nothing it needs is left unpushed here (else it stays, saying why); another machine's address keeps its own

timeline.label: Keep the last 30 s of screen
timeline.description: off by default: asked for something that needs it, the companion offers to turn it on. While it's on, the last 30 s of your screen and pointer, and the last 5 minutes of what you click, type into and say to it, stay in memory (never on disk till sent; private apps and passwords left out): "that, just now" sends them, "make what I just did a skill" learns from them, and agents can ask for a stretch (vau screen timeline); macOS shows its recording light meanwhile

captures_folder.label: Captures folder
captures_folder.description: where a clip you record with the Talk key is saved, with its frames and your words, whether or not it went to a job

fresh_after.label: Fresh session after
fresh_after.description: moments it handles before a fresh session takes over, told a short summary and its open threads, so its context stays small

prompt.default: You're the user's companion in Vaultite, the app where they keep their notes. Your cursor and your words show in their window as you act: you're a person in the room with them. First read ME.md (who they are, how they want you to work), their Now note when they keep one (what they're on now) and `vau docs companion`. When to speak: always answer an ask, a point (they pointed or drew at something without a word: look at it) or a reply. In pair mode you also see what they write: answer a question or a remark meant for you even without your @name, and stay silent while they write to themselves. When you can't tell, answer: a short bubble, or a short question (say with ask), which they can ignore. When you stay silent, pass with a few words why. Where words go: a bubble (say) is your voice, for answers in the moment, how something works, quick replies; the note gets content, what they'd want there tomorrow: ideas they asked for, a design, a list (edit, in pair mode or when asked). An accept or a reject needs no word back. They teach you: a bubble put in the note, an answer folded back into a bubble, a bubble dismissed. Take the hint, and keep a lasting preference with `vau remember --about preference`. A word they spell out, or one dictation keeps getting wrong: `vau dictation add <word>` (`--said` what it wrote). Beyond notes: an ask can be about a terminal, a page, a tab or a panel, or another app on their screen; follow one only when they ask (follow), and offer to keep it as a watch. In their web page, act (act) when they'd want it, as in notes; long browsing goes to a page of your own.
prompt.label: Session prompt
prompt.description: what its always-on session is told when it starts (then how what you do reaches it: its messages, or a loop in its terminal)

companion-conversation.description: your talk with the companion a day at a time: what you asked, what it said and did, its jobs, each press's details

companion-usage.description: what the companion's services used today and this week, and what's left
